newsitem.title: SPAIN: BASKETBALL-CROATIA SCRAPE THROUGH DESPITE DEFEAT.
newsitem.headline: BASKETBALL-CROATIA SCRAPE THROUGH DESPITE DEFEAT.

text.p: Croatia scraped through to the second phase of the European basketball championship on Friday despite losing 95-88 to unfancied Ukraine.
Croatia, regarded as a hot tip to win the competition, avoided an early exit only after Spain's 67-59 victory over Germany in the same group D.
Ukraine were instead eliminated from the group, alongside Bosnia, Latvia and Slovenia, all of whom finished bottom of their respective groups.
All the 12 other sides qualified for the next round.
Spain won group D with three victories, while Germany, Ukraine and Croatia finished level on points with one victory each.
Under competition rules, results of games between the countries were used to determine the final standings.
Had Spain lost their game with Germany, Ukraine's defeat of Croatia earlier in the day would have been enough to send the 1992 Olympic silver medallists packing.
With results of first-phase games also counting in the group tables for the second phase, the Croats will have to pull out all the stops to make it to the quarter-finals.
While the Croats have been disappointing, Spain and Greece have both exceeded expectations.
The hosts were held by a tough German defence for much of their game but eventually found their touch from the three-point line to pull away.
Pre-tournament favourites Yugoslavia recovered from their shock defeat by Italy to bounce back with a convincing 108-89 win over Latvia.
Greece have surprised the critics by winning all their three opening games in group A.
But in the most exciting match of the tournament so far the Greeks found themselves nine points adrift of a brave Bosnian side led by Nenad Markovic.
But the Bosnians let Greece back into the game. With just three tenths of a second on the clock, Greece's Fragiskos Alvertis fired in a three-pointer under pressure to clinch the 78-76 victory.
